work.title: Recovery method presentation across Analyze, Review, and workbook
authority: Direct user request to implement minimal Review/Analyze/workbook recovery method presentation without automatic weighting.

intent.productGoal: Make recovery-method evidence and governed professional judgment inspectable in the formula-driven QoR work product.
intent.capability: Present parallel recovery methods, evidence states, components, overrides, and the composite candidate/approval distinction in Analyze, Review, and the workbook.
architecturalIntent: The existing Method Profile and the reusable recovery engine remain separate until an explicit integration decision is made.
Observed A/R, method inputs, composite candidate, and professional approval remain distinct layers.
The workbook remains a formula-driven compilation of the exact run.
invariants: No automatic weighting or composite recovery rate is introduced.
Unconfigured rates remain explicitly unavailable rather than coerced to zero.
Professional approval is never inferred from a candidate or an engineering/synthetic profile.
acceptanceEvidence: Core workbook regression asserting recovery presentation and unchanged formulas.
Workbench syntax/typecheck after adding the Analyze and Review presentation.

decisions.decision: Present collection distribution, percent of charges, and composite as parallel, non-calculating rows.
decisions.rationale: It exposes method choice, evidence gaps, components, and override semantics without changing the legacy calculation or inventing automatic weighting.

decisions.decision: Present composite recovery as a governed candidate and state its override precedence.
decisions.rationale: A composite requires combination inputs, rationale, reviewer authority, and approval; its first matching segment override must not be mistaken for an automatic weighting policy.

observedBehaviour: Analyze injects a run-bound recovery-method presentation with parallel methods, evidence-state, components, override, and composite-boundary columns.
Review includes the same recovery-method boundary before the candidate queue.
The compiled workbook now includes Recovery Methods and preserves the legacy Recovery Analysis formulas and draft-release boundary.

evidence.result: 43/43 tests passed, including the workbook recovery-presentation regression and reusable recovery-method tests.
Passed Node syntax checks for the new recovery-method client module and existing workbench files.
Validated against the HiveForge conformance schema.

divergences.expected: Each displayed parallel method has run-bound recovery evidence and a persisted approval lifecycle.
divergences.observed: The reusable recovery engine is intentionally not wired into existing analysis runs; the presentation therefore labels the methods as not evaluated when no recovery-method record is attached.

learning.recurringPattern: A configured calculation profile cannot silently become a professional composite decision.
learning.improvementProposal: Integrate recovery-engine results and governed composite approvals only through a separately approved run-bound ledger contract.
durableKnowledge: Recovery-method presentation must not imply automatic weighting or professional approval.
First-match segment overrides are precedence rules, not weights.
